[EFFECT]
The day of the week has a non-monotonic, categorical effect on predicted hourly bike demand. Sunday (day 0) is by far the weakest day, pulling demand noticeably down (a contribution of about −0.065 in log space), while Monday is also slightly below neutral. From Tuesday onward demand climbs, peaking on **Friday** (day 5, contribution ≈ +0.041), then dipping slightly on Saturday (≈ +0.020). In practical terms, Friday typically sees the highest model-predicted demand, and Sunday the lowest, with the rest of the weekdays sitting somewhere in between.

[IMPORTANCE]
Weekday ranks **7th out of 9 features** in overall importance (importance score ≈ 0.024), making it a relatively minor driver of demand. The hour of the day (rank 1, score ≈ 0.89), temperature (rank 2), and year (rank 3) all exert far stronger influence, so the day-of-week effect is real but modest.

[RECOMMENDATION]
Since Friday consistently registers the highest predicted demand and Sunday the lowest, it is worth ensuring slightly higher bike availability and staff coverage on Fridays while accepting that Sunday operations can be leaner — but keep in mind that the time of day and weather conditions will still dominate any planning decisions.
